c36f23c0be: Giving feedback: one compliment, one question, one suggestion
bc00b80436: Name the lyric line or melody that moved you most, and why.
e8a6d2bfdf: What wasn't clear as you listened: the point of view, the plot, the meaning of a line.
0e3c161a57: A direction they can act on right away, such as repeating the chorus once or changing a word's tone.
17e8f2b77a: Feedback is about the song, not the person. Say "this line's rhyme feels a bit forced", not "you're bad at rhyming".
cd0ee1d3d5: BuildLearning to weigh others' criticism
7ebe1e677c: When you get feedback, first work out where it's coming from
19dbc8d400: Consider it seriouslyIt points out specific problems and reasons, and is usually worth taking on.
e980f74c07: Just as importantMost listeners are amateurs, and their impressions are closest to how the market will react.
26f47cabd6: Don't take it to heartCriticism with no reasons, only emotion, can't help your song.
ef48985b25: Stay level-headedIf your song gets under someone's skin, it has power.
cb2c5becee: Take it gladlyNote what people like; your style may be hiding there.
872b6c79d8: Rule of thumbWhen three or more people point out the same problem, it's time to rewrite.
f49aca1b2b: Practise today's feedback method on a classic first

96065934be: Shih Yi-lang sets the bustle of a wedding against the loneliness of loss, keeps one rhyme throughout, and builds the chorus step by step; Phil Chang's melody lifts the range in the chorus, releasing the pent-up emotion all at once. The scene, point of view and rhymes stay consistent throughout: a model of a well-built song.

9344bab5bf: True or false: ideas from the eight lessons
2b4b05a1fe: When setting lyrics you don't need to think about singability; that's the singer's job
df9be393a5: FalseSet lyrics to follow the melody's contour and the tones, to reduce clashes between words and music.
61923b4f5a: Setting music means composing to the content and sections of the lyrics
80f039c18f: TrueWords first, then music: that's setting music.
e1e46d0193: Analysing lyricists' techniques and rhetoric is an important reference for your own lyrics
0015fd4c2d: TrueAll art begins with imitation, and what you imitate is technique.
cc322d904a: A song is like a story and needs an opening, development, turn and close
a6039955a3: TrueThe verse tells the story, the pre-chorus builds the heat, the chorus releases it, and the outro wraps up.
73bd621928: Express what you really think; a bit negative or extreme is fine
b575b74197: FalseIdeas that are too negative or extreme are one of the nine taboos of lyrics.
4d38193f26: TrueA song talks to its listeners and records its era too.
a7be02ebbe: The essence of songwriting, sharing your work and self-fulfilment
3bac6d61bb: Record the details of life in melody and words, and carry what you feel and what moves you across whole into the listener's heart.
9d738b94e1: Only after you release a song does the conversation with the world really begin. Share it with friends, post it online, enter contests, and let more people hear it.
6488cb2e6c: Good music doesn't need a pile of advanced technique. Fully expressing what you feel is an art nobody can copy.
7cf5b939ce: The road of songwriting is long, and we'll always need each other's encouragement. Eight lessons are only the start; your next song begins with an idea tonight.
